lead: Anaemia is the commonest medical problem of pregnancy; iron deficiency causes 80–90%. It is Hb below 11 g/dL in the first trimester, below 10.5 in the second and third, and below 10 after birth. It makes haemorrhage, infection and heart failure more dangerous.
f: Grades and physiological anaemia

Mild 10–10.9 · moderate 7–9.9 · severe below 7 · very severe below 4 g/dL · Physiological anaemia: plasma rises faster than red cells; Hb 10.5–11 in the second trimester with normal MCV and ferritin: no treatment · Iron need about 1000 mg; folate need doubles

sc: Hb 10.6 at 24 wk, MCV normal, well → Physiological: reassure

f: Causes and risk factors

Deficiency: iron (commonest), folate (megaloblastic), B12 (rare) · Haemolytic: sickle cell, thalassaemia, G6PD, malaria · Blood loss: APH, miscarriage, hookworm, schistosomiasis · Chronic disease: TB, HIV, renal disease · Risk: poor diet, pica, tea with meals, high parity, short interval, twins, teenage pregnancy, anti-epileptics

sc: Pale, on phenytoin, large cells → Folate deficiency

f: Clinical features
Often none · Tired, dizzy, breathless; pica · Pallor, tachycardia, flow murmur · Iron lack: smooth tongue, koilonychia · Jaundice and spleen in haemolysis; S3 in failure
Investigations

First line: FBC + MCV, film, ferritin, malaria film or RDT, stool for ova, urine · No response: Hb electrophoresis, B12, folate, G6PD, renal, liver, thyroid, HIV, TB · Iron deficiency: low MCV, pencil cells, ferritin below 15, TIBC raised · Megaloblastic: high MCV, macro-ovalocytes, hypersegmented neutrophils · β-thal trait: MCV very low for the Hb, target cells, normal ferritin, HbA2 over 3.5% · Sickle: sickle cells, HbS · Mentzer index (MCV ÷ RBC): under 13 thal, over 13 iron

sc: No rise after 4 wk of iron, MCV 64, ferritin normal → Hb electrophoresis (thal trait)
tr: Small cells with normal ferritin = thal trait: do not give iron for months; ferritin also rises with infection

f: Types and their treatment

Megaloblastic: folic acid 5 mg + iron; low B12: hydroxocobalamin 1 mg IM first · Sickle cell (HbSS): crises, infection, VTE, FGR; folic acid 5 mg, no iron unless ferritin low, malaria prophylaxis, growth scans; crisis: fluids, O₂, analgesia, antibiotics, LMWH · Sickle trait: more UTIs · β-thal trait: folic acid 5 mg, iron only if ferritin low; two carriers: 25% major · G6PD: avoid sulphonamides, nitrofurantoin, primaquine
Complications
Mother: heart failure, PPH poorly tolerated, APH, sepsis, VTE · Baby: preterm birth, FGR, stillbirth, low iron stores · NTD from folate lack (not iron)
Prevention

Folic acid 0.4 mg before conception to 12 wk; 5 mg if high risk (previous NTD, anti-epileptics, diabetes, obesity, sickle cell, thal, twins) · Iron 30–60 mg + folate daily from booking to 3 months after birth · Hb at booking, 28 and 36 wk · Treat malaria and hookworm, bed nets, space births
Oral and parenteral iron

Ferrous sulphate 200 mg (65 mg iron) 2–3 times daily: first choice, black stool · Take 1 h before food with vitamin C; not with tea, milk or antacids · Response: reticulocytes rise at 7–10 days, Hb rises about 1 g/dL a week; recheck at 3 wk; continue 3 months after Hb is normal · Parenteral iron: intolerance, non-adherence, malabsorption, or Hb 7–9.9 after about 34 wk; not in the first trimester · Iron sucrose 200 mg IV 2–3 times a week: safest · Iron dextran: test dose, adrenaline ready

sc: Hb 8.5 at 35 wk, vomits oral iron → IV iron sucrose
No rise on iron, takes it with tea → Correct how she takes it

f: Blood transfusion

Hb below 7 before 36 wk, no failure: admit, find the cause, oral or IV iron · Hb below 7 after 36 wk: transfuse (no time for iron) · Heart failure or Hb below 5: transfuse at any gestation · Also with bleeding, sepsis, labour or CS due · Packed cells, 1 unit over 3–4 h, furosemide 20–40 mg IV if overload risk · Observe every 15 min at first; stop for breathlessness, crackles or fever · Aim for safety (Hb about 8), not full correction

sc: Para 8, 37 wk, Hb 6, breathless, MCV 58 → Slow packed cells with furosemide

f: Labour and puerperium

Hospital birth, 2 units cross-matched, IV line, semi-sitting, careful fluids · Shorten the second stage if tired · Active third stage (oxytocin 10 IU IM); replace loss early · Iron for 3 months, family planning
